summary: Syntax and imports are fine, and the simulation generally runs. However, calibration logic reuses the same simulator instance without resetting or windowing metrics, leading to accumulating state and NaN scores during calibration. Micro-transition capture defaults to on and can cause heavy memory/IO. Some parameter override handling bypasses registry validation.

issues.description: Calibration/evaluation reuses the same Simulation instance across trials without resetting state. Subsequent runs append to the same observables and alter internal state, corrupting metrics and comparisons.
issues.solution: Instantiate a fresh Simulation per evaluation (e.g., build a new Simulation with the same params) or implement a Simulation.reset() method to reinitialize state before each run.

issues.description: Metrics are computed against full-length ground truth while only a window is simulated, causing length mismatch and NaN RMSE. This results in NaN scores during calibration.
issues.solution: Compute metrics on the specified window by slicing both simulated observables and ground truth to the same [start:end] range, or extend Simulation.evaluate() to accept a window argument and use it for consistent comparisons.

issues.description: Micro-transition capture is enabled by default and records potentially very large numbers of records (O(N*days)), which can cause high memory usage and large JSON outputs.
issues.location: Simulation._init_population() sets 'capture_micro': True; InfluencePropagation.forward() appends to 'micro.transitions'
issues.solution: Default 'capture_micro' to False or add a parameter to control sampling rate (e.g., record a random subset) and gate saving under QUICK_TEST or explicit CLI flag.

issues.description: CLI overrides are applied directly to the registry values, bypassing unknown-key checks and set_params() warnings.
issues.solution: Use ParameterRegistry.set_params() to apply overrides and handle unknown/frozen keys consistently; report and persist warnings.

issues.description: Observation aggregator both mutates state and returns outputs that are committed again, creating overlapping responsibilities and a brittle coupling.
issues.solution: Have the aggregator compute and return outputs only; avoid mutating state inside module, or centralize all state mutation in Simulation.run().

issues.description: Potentially large module I/O dumps including all micro-transition records may cause big JSON files and slow writes.
issues.solution: Compress large I/O (e.g., gzip), limit saved fields, or sample records; optionally add a size cap or a flag to disable saving micro transitions.

issues.description: Some fields are unused or weakly enforced (e.g., parameter bounds not applied, media_exposure/household norm_strength unused).
issues.solution: Enforce bounds when applying parameters and remove or utilize unused fields, or document them as placeholders.
Remove unused imports to reduce lint warnings.
